# Load Data

```{r load-libraries, include=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cmdstanr)
library(here)
library(matrixStats)
library(survey)
library(sampling)
```

We'll set a few parameters for the test run here:

```{r set-params}
alpha <- 0.05
mcmc_iter <- 1000
mcmc_burn <- 1000
curr_seed <- 100

scale_nps_prior_weight_covariate <- TRUE
n_chains <- 2
mcmc_threads_per_chain <- 1
nps_prior_which <- c("pp", "md", "mdl", "mdl10")
```

```{r regenerate-samples, eval = FALSE}
source(here::here("code", "tests", "create_test_sample.R"))
```

```{r load-samples}
# Load the generated samples
load(here::here("data", "test_sample.RData"), verbose = TRUE)

# Load and factor population for comparisons (matches main.R)
acs_pop <- read_csv(here::here("data", "ACS_NPS_pop.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    AGEP_binned = factor(AGEP_binned),
    RAC1P = factor(RAC1P),
    SEX = factor(SEX),
    PUMA = factor(PUMA)
  )
```

We want the default weights to sum to the population, but some methods will require them to sum to the sample size.

```{r check_weights}
ps_df$weights <-  nrow(acs_pop) * ps_df$weights / sum(ps_df$weights)
ps_scale_weights <- nrow(ps_df) * ps_df$weights / sum(ps_df$weights)

cat("Rescaled weights add up to:", sum(ps_scale_weights), "\n")
cat("Weights add up to:", sum(ps_df$weights), "\n")
cat("Population N: ", nrow(acs_pop), "\n")
``` 

Set covariates and random effect variables:

```{r setup-covs}
X_formula   <- as.formula("~ AGEP_binned + RAC1P + SEX")

X_ps <- model.matrix(X_formula, data = ps_df)
y_ps <- ps_df$PUBCOV

X_nps <- model.matrix(X_formula, data = nps_df)
y_nps <- nps_df$PUBCOV
```

# Data Overview

```{r overview, include=FALSE}
data.frame(
  Sample = c("Population", "PS", "NPS"),
  N = c(nrow(acs_pop), nrow(ps_df), nrow(nps_df)),
  PUBCOV_Rate = c(mean(acs_pop$PUBCOV), mean(ps_df$PUBCOV), mean(nps_df$PUBCOV))
) %>%
    mutate(PUBCOV_Rate = round(PUBCOV_Rate, 3))
```

# Model Specification

We observe a probability sample (PS) \((y_i, \mathbf{x}_i)\) for \(i = 1,\ldots,n\) and a nonprobability sample (NPS) \((\tilde{y}_\ell, \tilde{\mathbf{x}}_\ell)\) for \(\ell = 1,\ldots,\tilde{n}\). The logistic model is

\[
y_i \mid \boldsymbol{\beta} \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\theta_i), \qquad 
\theta_i = \frac{\exp(\mathbf{x}_i'\boldsymbol{\beta})}{1 + \exp(\mathbf{x}_i'\boldsymbol{\beta})}.
\]

so each likelihood contribution is 

\[
p(y_i \mid {\beta}) = \frac{\exp({x}_i'{\beta})^{y_i}}{[1 + \exp({x}_i'{\beta})]}
\]

## Pseudolikelihood

Given weights $w_1, \ldots, w_n$ equal to the inverse probabilities of selection in the PS after rescaling to sum to the sample 
size $n$, we exponentiate the likelihood contributions as 

\[
\tilde{p}(y_i \mid {\beta}) = \frac{\exp({x}_i'{\beta})^{w_i y_i}}{[1 + \exp({x}_i'{\beta})]^{w_i}}
\]

A likelihood-based model is recovered by setting each weight to 1.

## Mixed-Distance Priors: General Form

The general form is

\[
\boldsymbol{\beta} \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{NPS}, \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\ldots,\sigma_p^2)).
\]

### HMC Implementation

We target the log posterior

\[
\log p(\beta \mid \cdot) =
\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i \log \text{Bernoulli}\left(y_i \mid \text{logit}^{-1}(x_i'\beta)\right)
\, + \,
\log \mathcal{N}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{NPS}, \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\ldots,\sigma_p^2)).
\]

Equivalently, using the logit link, the log-likelihood terms are

\[
\log p(y_i \mid \beta) = y_i (x_i'\beta) - \log\{1 + \exp(x_i'\beta)\}
\]

```{stanmodel, eval = FALSE}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;                    // PS sample size
  int<lower=1> p;                    // number of predictors
  int<lower=1> J;                    // number of domains

  matrix[n, p] X;                    // PS design matrix

  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[n] y;  // PS outcomes

  vector<lower=0>[n] w;              // PS weights (rescaled to sum to n)

  vector[p] beta_prior_mean;         // beta hat NPS (will calculate in R)
  vector<lower=0>[p] beta_prior_sd;  // sigma_j

  array[n] int<lower=1, upper=J> domain; // PS domain indices
}

parameters {
  vector[p] beta;
  vector[J] z_domain;
  real<lower=0> sigma_domain;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[J] eta_domain;
  eta_domain = sigma_domain * z_domain; // non-centered for better efficiency
}

model {
  // Prior
  beta ~ normal(beta_prior_mean, beta_prior_sd);
  sigma_domain ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  z_domain ~ normal(0, 1);

  // Pseudolikelihood (only PS) (vectorized)
  vector[n] eta = X * beta + eta_domain[domain]; // linear predictor
  target += dot_product(w, y .* eta - log1p_exp(eta));
}
```

We fit this model for each of the three following variations on the mixed-distance prior.

### Mixed-Distance

\[
\sigma_j = |\hat{\beta}_{PS,j} - \hat{\beta}_{NPS,j}|.
\]

### Mixed-Distance-log

\[
\sigma_j = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\log \tilde{n}} \max\{(\hat{\beta}_{PS,j}-\hat{\beta}_{NPS,j})^2,\, \hat{\sigma}^2_{NPS,j}\}}.
\]

### Mixed-Distance-log10

\[
\sigma_j = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\log_{10} \tilde{n}} \max\{(\hat{\beta}_{PS,j}-\hat{\beta}_{NPS,j})^2,\, \hat{\sigma}^2_{NPS,j}\}}.
\]


## Power Prior

A power prior on $\beta$ is

\[
p(\beta \mid \tilde{y}, \tilde{X}) \propto L(\beta \mid \tilde{y},\tilde{X})^a \, p(\beta),
\]

with a fixed exponent \(a\). The authors set \(a\) equal to the \(p\)-value resulting from a 
Hotelling \(T^2\) test of equality between \(\hat{\beta}_{PS}\) and \(\hat{\beta}_{NPS}\). They also 
place a \(t_3(0, 2.5)\) prior on each coefficient, resulting in the 
posterior distribution
\[
p(\beta \mid \text{data}) \propto 
\left\{ \prod_{i = 1}^n \frac{\exp({x}_i'{\beta})^{w_i y_i}}{[1 + \exp({x}_i'{\beta})]^{w_i}}  \right\}
\left\{ \prod_{\ell = 1}^{\tilde{n}} \frac{\exp(\tilde{x}_\ell'{\beta})^{a \tilde{y}_\ell}}{[1 + \exp(\tilde{x}_\ell'{\beta})]^{a}} \right\} 
\left\{\prod_{j=1}^p t_3(\beta_j \mid 0, 2.5)\right\}
\]

### HMC Implementation 

In the Stan implementation, we target the following log posterior:

\[
\log p(\beta \mid \cdot) =
\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i \log \text{Bernoulli}\left(y_i \mid \text{logit}^{-1}(x_i'\beta)\right)
\, + \,
a \sum_{\ell=1}^{\tilde{n}} \log \text{Bernoulli}\left(\tilde{y}_\ell \mid \text{logit}^{-1}(\tilde{x}_\ell'\beta)\right)
\, + \,
\sum_{j=1}^{p} \log t_3(\beta_j \mid 0, 2.5).
\]

Equivalently, using the logit link, the log-likelihood terms are

\[
\log p(y_i \mid \beta) = y_i (x_i'\beta) - \log\{1 + \exp(x_i'\beta)\},
\qquad
\log p(\tilde{y}_\ell \mid \beta) = \tilde{y}_\ell (\tilde{x}_\ell'\beta) - \log\{1 + \exp(\tilde{x}_\ell'\beta)\}.
\]

```{stanmodel, eval = FALSE}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;                 // PS sample size
  int<lower=1> n_np;              // NPS sample size
  int<lower=1> p;                 // number of coefficients
  int<lower=1> J;                 // number of domains

  matrix[n, p] X;                 // PS design matrix
  matrix[n_np, p] X_np;           // NPS design matrix

  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[n] y;        // PS outcomes
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[n_np] y_np;   // NPS outcomes

  vector<lower=0>[n] w;           // PS weights (rescaled to sum to n)
  real<lower=0, upper=1> a;       // power prior exponent

  array[n] int<lower=1, upper=J> domain;       // PS domain indices
  array[n_np] int<lower=1, upper=J> domain_np; // NPS domain indices
}

parameters {
  vector[p] beta;
  vector[J] z_domain;
  real<lower=0> sigma_domain;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[J] eta_domain;
  eta_domain = sigma_domain * z_domain; // non-centered for better efficiency
}

model {
  // Prior: t_3(0, 2.5)
  beta ~ student_t(3, 0, 2.5);
  sigma_domain ~ normal(0, 1);
  z_domain ~ normal(0, 1);

  // PS pseudolikelihood (vectorized)
  vector[n] eta = X * beta + eta_domain[domain]; // linear predictor
  target += dot_product(w, y .* eta - log1p_exp(eta));

  // NPS likelihood (power prior) (vectorized)
  vector[n_np] eta_np = X_np * beta + eta_domain[domain_np];
  target += a * (y_np .* eta_np - log1p_exp(eta_np));
}
```

# Import the model 

```{r import-model}
nps_prior_md_mod <- cmdstan_model(
  file.path("code", "models", "nps_prior_md.stan"),
  cpp_options = list(stan_threads = TRUE)
)

nps_prior_pp_mod <- cmdstan_model(
  file.path("code", "models", "nps_prior_pp.stan"),
  cpp_options = list(stan_threads = TRUE)
)

# R script which pre-processes data to feed into Stan
# and post-processes Stan output
source(here::here("code", "models", "nps_prior.R"))
```

This model requires some metadata to aggregate unit-level predictions to area-level:

```{r helper-data}
domain_levels <- sort(unique(c(as.character(ps_df$PUMA), as.character(nps_df$PUMA))))
domain_ps <- match(ps_df$PUMA, domain_levels)
domain_nps <- match(nps_df$PUMA, domain_levels)
PUMA_levels <- domain_levels
```

We first calculate the power prior exponent:

```{r pp-a}
power_prior_a <- NULL
if ("pp" %in% nps_prior_which) {
  power_prior_a <- calculate_adaptive_power_prior_a(
    y_ps = y_ps,
    X_ps = X_ps,
    y_nps = y_nps,
    X_nps = X_nps,
    verbose = TRUE
  )$a
}
```

# Results

The original paper uses design weights as a covariate. To create weights for the NPS, we follow the authors in raking to population 
benchmarks:

```{r rak}
# Raked weights for weight-as-covariate prior
rake_vars <- c("AGEP_binned", "RAC1P", "SEX")
pop_margins <- lapply(rake_vars, function(v) {
  as.data.frame(table(acs_pop[[v]])) %>%
    rename(!!v := Var1, Freq = Freq)
})
nps_design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, data = nps_df, weights = ~1)
rake_formulas <- lapply(rake_vars, function(v) as.formula(paste0("~", v)))
nps_raked_design <- rake(
  design = nps_design,
  sample.margins = rake_formulas,
  population.margins = pop_margins
)
nps_rake_weights <- weights(nps_raked_design)
nps_rake_weights <- length(nps_rake_weights) * nps_rake_weights / sum(nps_rake_weights)
```

We then sample from the posterior distribution and aggregate to area-level predictions:

```{r fit-rak, results = 'hide', message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
nps_prior_rak_res <- nps_prior_mcmc(
  md_mod = nps_prior_md_mod,
  pp_mod = nps_prior_pp_mod,
  y = y_ps,
  X = X_ps,
  y_NP = y_nps,
  X_NP = X_nps,
  wts = NULL,
  PUMA = factor(ps_df$PUMA, levels = domain_levels),
  PUMA_levels = PUMA_levels,
  raking_or_pl = "Raking",
  typeIerr = alpha,
  niter = mcmc_iter,
  warmup = mcmc_burn,
  chains = n_chains,
  seed = curr_seed,
  which_prior = nps_prior_which,
  a = power_prior_a,
  domain_ps = domain_ps,
  domain_nps = domain_nps,
  domain_levels = domain_levels,
  weight_covariate = list(ps = ps_scale_weights, nps = nps_rake_weights),
  scale_weight_covariate = scale_nps_prior_weight_covariate,
  threads_per_chain = mcmc_threads_per_chain,
  parallel_chains = n_chains
)
```

```{r save-rak, include = FALSE}
saveRDS(nps_prior_rak_res, here::here("data", "nps_prior_rak_res.RDS"))
```

We can also incorporate the design weights using a pseudolikelihood:

```{r fit-pl, results = 'hide', message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
nps_prior_pl_res <- nps_prior_mcmc(
  md_mod = nps_prior_md_mod,
  pp_mod = nps_prior_pp_mod,
  y = y_ps,
  X = X_ps,
  y_NP = y_nps,
  X_NP = X_nps,
  wts = ps_scale_weights,
  PUMA = factor(ps_df$PUMA, levels = domain_levels),
  PUMA_levels = PUMA_levels,
  raking_or_pl = "Pseudolikelihood",
  typeIerr = alpha,
  niter = mcmc_iter,
  warmup = mcmc_burn,
  chains = n_chains,
  seed = curr_seed,
  which_prior = nps_prior_which,
  a = power_prior_a,
  domain_ps = domain_ps,
  domain_nps = domain_nps,
  domain_levels = domain_levels,
  threads_per_chain = mcmc_threads_per_chain,
  parallel_chains = n_chains
)
```

```{r save-pl, include = FALSE}
saveRDS(nps_prior_pl_res, here::here("data", "nps_prior_pl_res.RDS"))
```

# Performance Comparison

## Calculate True Values and Direct Estimates

```{r true-values}
# Calculate true population values by PUMA (what we're trying to estimate)
true_values <- acs_pop %>%
  group_by(PUMA) %>%
  summarize(
    response_true = mean(PUBCOV, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r direct-estimates}
# Create survey design
samp.design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~weights, data = ps_df)

# svyby extraction: use built-in se to avoid manual column juggling
direst <- svyby(
  ~PUBCOV,
  ~PUMA,
  samp.design,
  svymean,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  vartype = "se",
  keep.names = FALSE
) %>%
  arrange(PUMA) %>%
  transmute(
    PUMA,
    point_est = PUBCOV, # pulling the mean column from svyby
    lower_CI = point_est + qnorm(alpha / 2) * se,
    upper_CI = point_est + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se,
    model = "direst"
  )
```

## Calculate Performance Metrics

```{r performance-metrics}
# Helper function for interval score (from main.R)
int_score <- function(alpha, truth, L, U){
  return(
    (U - L) + 
        2/alpha*(truth < L)*(L - truth) + 
        2/alpha*(truth > U)*(truth - U)
  )
}

# Combine your model results with direct estimates
all_results <- bind_rows(
    direst,
    nps_prior_pl_res, 
    nps_prior_rak_res
)

# Calculate performance metrics for all models
performance_metrics <- true_values %>%
  left_join(all_results, by = "PUMA") %>% 
  mutate(model = ifelse(model=="direst", "baseline_HT", model)) %>% 
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarize(
    MSE = mean((response_true - point_est)^2),
    MAB = mean(abs(response_true - point_est)),
    Coverage = mean(between(response_true, lower_CI, upper_CI)),
    `Int. Score` = mean(int_score(alpha, response_true, lower_CI, upper_CI)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

performance_metrics
```

## Visualize Estimates vs Truth

```{r visualize}
# Plot estimates vs truth for direct estimates and NPS Prior Models
ggplot(true_values %>% left_join(all_results, by = "PUMA"),
       aes(x = response_true, y = point_est)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_CI, ymax = upper_CI), alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Direct Estimates vs True PUMA Values",
    x = "True PUBCOV Rate",
    y = "Estimated PUBCOV Rate"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~model) + 
  theme_bw()

ggsave("nps_prior_res.pdf", width = 12.4, height = 7)
```
